newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Easy Knit plans expansion in retailing.
newsitem.headline: Easy Knit plans expansion in retailing.

text.p: Hong Kong-based Easyknit International Holdings Ltd plans to use the proceeds from its initial public offering in Singapore to expand its retail operations, senior company officials said on Friday.
The company, which exports cotton-based garments for women, children and infants, is offering 45 million new shares at Hong Kong $3.05 (US$0.39) each in its secondary listing in Singapore.
Officials said of the HK$128.8 million net proceeds, HK$100 million would finance expansion of the group's retail operations, mainly in Hong Kong.
They said they would use HK$5 million to establish sourcing offices in Singapore and Indonesia and the remaining HK$23.8 million as additional working capital.

Officials said Easyknit, which has the franchise for France's Renoma S.T.A.R. in Hong Kong, planned to use Renoma as a springboard into the retail sector. Its first outlet in Hong Kong opened in September.

"We believe this move into higher margin retail sales will be successful as we are leveraging on our existing stengths and resources, on our designs and manufacturing abilities and on our knowledge of retail markets," president and chief executive officer Matthew Koon said.

"We believe the expansion...into retailing will provide the group with an additional source of income," Koon said. He added that the group's margins would be raised by 50 percent from its entry into the Hong Kong retail market.
"We hope our retail business will contribute as much as our export and sourcing business in the future," vice president Alan Tsang said.

Tsang said the company plans to negotiate for a master license in 1997 to manufacture and retail Renoma in Hong Kong, Taiwan and China at a later date. Tsang said there are no plans to enter into other franchises at the moment.
Easyknit will launch its own brand name of casual fashion wear under "Library" in Hong Kong next March.
"We are confident by the first year of the launch of Library, we will see some returns in our retail business," Tsang added.
He added that Easyknit would continue to concentrate on its core business of sourcing and export and intended to diversify into higher value-added garments like children and infant wear.
Tsang said the group hoped its secondary listing in Singapore would give them a higher profile and expand its investor base in the region.
